easy.question: Who spoke to Moses?
answers: The Lord
Aaron
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “And the Lord spake unto Moses.”

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak?
answers: To Aaron
To Moses
To the children of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse states that the Lord spoke to Moses.

easy.question: Which verb describes the Lord’s action in the verse?
answers: He heard
He walked
He spoke
easy.explanation: The phrase “spake unto Moses” describes the Lord’s action.

medium.question: What can be understood from the fact that the Lord spoke to Moses?
answers: Moses received a message from the Lord
Moses spoke to the Lord first
Moses set out on a journey
medium.explanation: The verse describes a message coming from the Lord to Moses.

medium.question: In the phrase “And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,” what does “saying” introduce?
answers: A command to walk
The words or message that follow
A command to be silent
medium.explanation: The word “saying” introduces the content of what will be spoken.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Moses speaks, and then the Lord listens
The Lord is silent, and then Moses speaks
The Lord speaks to Moses, and then a message is given
medium.explanation: First the Lord speaks to Moses; the word “saying” points ahead to the message that follows.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the direct address to Moses?
answers: Moses serves as the recipient and messenger of the message
Moses is the author of the Lord’s words
Moses has no connection to the message
challenge.explanation: Addressing the words to Moses shows that he receives the message and is to convey it or act on it.

challenge.question: What is distinctive about the structure “spake ... saying”?
answers: It describes only a physical action
It presents speech followed by the content of the message
It describes a conversation between two equal speakers
challenge.explanation: “Spake” identifies the act of speaking, while “saying” introduces the content of the words.

challenge.question: Which detail in the verse emphasizes the direction of the message?
answers: The word “Moses” proves that Moses spoke
The word “saying” proves that the message ended
The phrase “unto Moses” shows that the speech was directed to Moses
challenge.explanation: The phrase “unto Moses” shows that the speech was directed from the speaker to Moses.

paragraphs.title: Purification After Giving Birth to a Son

easy.question: How many days is the woman unclean after giving birth to a son?
answers: Seven days
Eight days
Thirty-three days
easy.explanation: The verse says that she shall be unclean seven days.

easy.question: What is done to the child on the eighth day?
answers: He is brought to the sanctuary
He is circumcised
He is purified
easy.explanation: The verse says, “in the eighth day ... he shall be circumcised.”

easy.question: What must the woman avoid during her purification period?
answers: Eating bread
Speaking with people
Touching holy things and entering the sanctuary
easy.explanation: She may touch no hallowed thing and may not enter the sanctuary until her purification days are fulfilled.

medium.question: What is the correct order after the birth of a son?
answers: Seven days of uncleanness, circumcision on the eighth day, and then thirty-three days of purification
Circumcision immediately, followed by seven days of uncleanness, and then the sanctuary
Thirty-three days of purification, followed by circumcision and seven days of uncleanness
medium.explanation: The passage presents seven days first, circumcision on the eighth day, and then thirty-three days of purification.

medium.question: In the sentence “If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child,” what does the phrase describe?
answers: Coming to the sanctuary
Conceiving and giving birth
Being purified with water
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a woman who has conceived and given birth to a male child.

medium.question: Why does the woman not enter the sanctuary immediately after giving birth?
answers: Because the child is not yet eight days old
Because she must bring an offering that same day
Because her purification days have not yet ended
medium.explanation: The verse says she may not enter the sanctuary until her purification days are fulfilled.

challenge.question: How many days does the entire period described after the birth of a son last, when the periods are counted consecutively?
answers: Forty days
Thirty-three days
Forty-one days
challenge.explanation: There are seven days of uncleanness plus thirty-three days of purification, making forty days.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that circumcision occurs on the eighth day while the purification period continues?
answers: Circumcision cancels all the purification days
Circumcision takes place before all the purification restrictions have ended
Circumcision occurs only after entering the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: Circumcision occurs on the eighth day, but thirty-three more days of purification remain.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “until the days of her purifying be fulfilled” show about the duration of the restrictions?
answers: They last throughout her life
They apply only on the day of birth
They end when the appointed period is complete
challenge.explanation: The word “until” sets a time limit, so the restrictions last only until the purification period is complete.

questions.question: How many days does the entire period described after the birth of a son last, when the periods are counted consecutively?
answers: Forty days
Thirty-three days
Forty-one days
questions.explanation: There are seven days of uncleanness plus thirty-three days of purification, making forty days.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that circumcision occurs on the eighth day while the purification period continues?
answers: Circumcision cancels all the purification days
Circumcision takes place before all the purification restrictions have ended
Circumcision occurs only after entering the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Circumcision occurs on the eighth day, but thirty-three more days of purification remain.

questions.question: What does the phrase “until the days of her purifying be fulfilled” show about the duration of the restrictions?
answers: They last throughout her life
They apply only on the day of birth
They end when the appointed period is complete
questions.explanation: The word “until” sets a time limit, so the restrictions last only until the purification period is complete.

paragraphs.title: Purification After Giving Birth to a Daughter

easy.question: If a daughter is born, how long is the woman unclean?
answers: Two weeks
Sixty days
One year
easy.explanation: The verse says that she shall be unclean for two weeks.

easy.question: What kind of child is described in the verse?
answers: A son
A daughter
Twins
easy.explanation: The verse says, “if she bear a maid child,” meaning if a daughter is born.

easy.question: How long does she continue in the blood of her purification after the two weeks?
answers: Seven days
Forty days
Sixty-six days
easy.explanation: After the two weeks, the verse specifies sixty-six days.

medium.question: What is the total period described, from the uncleanness until the end of the purification period?
answers: Eighty days
Sixty-six days
Seventy days
medium.explanation: Two weeks equal fourteen days, and fourteen plus sixty-six equals eighty days.

medium.question: In the phrase “she shall continue in the blood of her purifying,” what does “continue” mean?
answers: She travels
She remains or waits
She eats
medium.explanation: In this context, “continue” means that she remains in that condition throughout the appointed period.

medium.question: What sequence of times is described in the verse?
answers: Sixty-six days, followed by two weeks
Two weeks only
Two weeks, followed by sixty-six days
medium.explanation: First she is unclean for two weeks, and afterward she continues for sixty-six days.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “as in her separation” show about the two-week period?
answers: It compares the period to her menstrual separation
It requires her to wait a year
It is unrelated to any specific period
challenge.explanation: The phrase compares her period of uncleanness with the period of her separation.

challenge.question: What number results from adding “threescore and six days”?
answers: Sixty days
Sixty-six days
Seventy-six days
challenge.explanation: “Threescore” means sixty, and six more makes sixty-six days.

challenge.question: What important distinction exists between the two parts of the verse?
answers: Both parts describe exactly the same period
The first part concerns a son and the second a daughter
The first describes uncleanness, and the second a period of continued purification
challenge.explanation: The verse distinguishes the two-week period of uncleanness from the following period of purification.

questions.question: What does the phrase “as in her separation” show about the two-week period?
answers: It compares the period to her menstrual separation
It requires her to wait a year
It is unrelated to any specific period
questions.explanation: The phrase compares her period of uncleanness with the period of her separation.

questions.question: What number results from adding “threescore and six days”?
answers: Sixty days
Sixty-six days
Seventy-six days
questions.explanation: “Threescore” means sixty, and six more makes sixty-six days.

questions.question: What important distinction exists between the two parts of the verse?
answers: Both parts describe exactly the same period
The first part concerns a son and the second a daughter
The first describes uncleanness, and the second a period of continued purification
questions.explanation: The verse distinguishes the two-week period of uncleanness from the following period of purification.

easy.question: When does the woman bring the offerings?
answers: After her purification days are complete
Before the birth
Only after one year
easy.explanation: The verse says, “when the days of her purifying are fulfilled,” meaning after they are complete.

easy.question: Which animals are mentioned for the offerings?
answers: A goat and a ram
A lamb and a young pigeon or turtledove
A bull and a calf
easy.explanation: The verse names a lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for a sin offering.

easy.question: To whom does the woman bring the offering?
answers: To the king
To the judge
To the priest
easy.explanation: She brings it to the door of the tabernacle, to the priest.

medium.question: What is the sequence of events described in the verses?
answers: The purification days end, offerings are brought and offered, and she is cleansed
Offerings are made, then the birth occurs, followed by purification days
She is cleansed, gives birth, and then brings offerings
medium.explanation: First the purification days end; then the offerings are brought and the priest offers them.

medium.question: In the phrase “when the days of her purifying are fulfilled,” what does “fulfilled” mean?
answers: When the purification days begin
When the purification days are completed
When the purification days are canceled
medium.explanation: “Fulfilled” means completed; here it refers to the end of the purification period.

medium.question: Who is covered by the law described in the verses?
answers: Only a woman who gives birth to a son
Only a woman who gives birth to a daughter
A woman who gives birth to either a son or a daughter
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly says the law applies whether the child is male or female.

challenge.question: What is the difference between the two offerings mentioned in the passage?
answers: The lamb is for a burnt offering, and the bird is for a sin offering
Both are sin offerings, but one is larger
The lamb is for a sin offering, and the bird is for a burnt offering
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly assigns the lamb to the burnt offering and the bird to the sin offering.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “cleansed from the issue of her blood” refer to?
answers: The location of the tabernacle
The mother’s bleeding
The blood of the sacrificial animals
challenge.explanation: The phrase concerns the woman’s purification and refers to her bleeding, not to the sacrificial blood.

challenge.question: Who is the person described by the words “make an atonement for her; and she shall be cleansed”?
answers: The child
The priest
The mother
challenge.explanation: The pronoun “her” refers to the woman who gave birth, the one who is cleansed.

questions.question: What is the difference between the two offerings mentioned in the passage?
answers: The lamb is for a burnt offering, and the bird is for a sin offering
Both are sin offerings, but one is larger
The lamb is for a sin offering, and the bird is for a burnt offering
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly assigns the lamb to the burnt offering and the bird to the sin offering.

questions.question: What does the phrase “cleansed from the issue of her blood” refer to?
answers: The location of the tabernacle
The mother’s bleeding

questions.explanation: The phrase concerns the woman’s purification and refers to her bleeding, not to the sacrificial blood.

questions.question: Who is the person described by the words “make an atonement for her; and she shall be cleansed”?
answers: The child
The priest
The mother
questions.explanation: The pronoun “her” refers to the woman who gave birth, the one who is cleansed.

paragraphs.title: The Offering of a Poor Woman

easy.question: What must she bring if she cannot afford a lamb?
answers: Two turtledoves or two young pigeons
Two lambs
A grain offering only
easy.explanation: The verse says that if she cannot bring a lamb, she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons.

easy.question: What is one of the birds used for?
answers: Atonement only
A burnt offering
Purification only
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the one for the burnt offering, and the other for a sin offering.”

easy.question: Who makes atonement for her according to the verse?
answers: The woman herself
Her family
The priest
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the priest shall make an atonement for her.”

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the verse?
answers: The priest cleanses her, and then the offering is brought
Two birds are brought, the priest makes atonement, and then she is clean
A lamb is brought, and then she brings birds
medium.explanation: The two birds are brought first; afterward the priest makes atonement, and she is declared clean.

medium.question: In the phrase “if she be not able to bring a lamb,” what does it mean?
answers: Her hand is not clean
She cannot find her hand
She lacks the means to obtain or pay for a lamb
medium.explanation: The context shows that she cannot afford or otherwise obtain a lamb.

medium.question: Why are two birds brought instead of one?
answers: Each bird has a different purpose: one is for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering
One bird is forbidden for sacrifice
The priest must eat one of them
medium.explanation: The verse assigns a different purpose to each of the two birds.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the option of bringing birds instead of a lamb?
answers: Everyone must bring both a lamb and birds
Birds are intended only for wealthy people
The law provides an alternative offering for someone unable to bring a lamb
challenge.explanation: The birds are presented as a substitute when the woman cannot bring a lamb.

challenge.question: Which detail might be missed in a quick reading of the verse?
answers: Each of the two animals has a different purpose
The priest has no role in the offering
Three birds are brought
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that one bird is for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering.

challenge.question: What change is described at the end of the verse?
answers: She becomes wealthy
After the priest makes atonement, she is clean
She becomes a priestess
challenge.explanation: The verse ends by saying that the priest makes atonement for her and she is clean.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the option of bringing birds instead of a lamb?
answers: Everyone must bring both a lamb and birds

The law provides an alternative offering for someone unable to bring a lamb
questions.explanation: The birds are presented as a substitute when the woman cannot bring a lamb.

questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that one bird is for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering.

questions.explanation: The verse ends by saying that the priest makes atonement for her and she is clean.
